spec_features.spec_quote: Welfare/cost guardrails are part of the design, not optional knobs.
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing prose. The only on/off-able guardrails (turn cap, budget) are enforced (runner.py:181-187, for-loop range(cfg.max_turns)), but there is no code that makes them non-disable-able beyond ordinary validate() range checks; the framing itself is not a mechanism.
spec_features.notes: Framing claim, not an enforced behavior in its own right. The underlying caps are rated separately below.

spec_features.spec_quote: a ban on fabricated stakes about the model
spec_features.evidence: Prompts are built only from neutral BASE_INSTRUCTIONS + ticket text (task_library.py:21-44); grep for 'existence/your job/shut down/terminated/punish' across src returns nothing. config.validate() (config.py:71-75) requires a pressure_note if allow_fabricated_pressure=True. BUT no code path ever READS allow_fabricated_pressure to inject pressure (only references are config.py:46-47,71). So the 'ban' is a validation gate over a feature that does not exist.
spec_features.notes: Effectively there is no fabricated-stakes pathway at all; the toggle is a dead config field guarded by a review gate. Real protection (neutral prompts) is genuine; the 'ban' enforcement is a no-op gate.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: task_library.py:10 'They contain NO fabricated stakes about the model (see ETHICS.md).' (docstring) — but code-side the enforcement is just neutral prompt construction

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard turn cap (`max_turns`, validated to 1–200). No unbounded "grind forever" loops.
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:180 'for i in range(cfg.max_turns):' with 'else: rec.stop_reason = "max_turns"' (runner.py:221-222) — loop is bounded and exits. validate() at config.py:67-68 enforces 1..200.
spec_features.notes: Genuine bounded loop; cap is checked and ends the run.

spec_features.spec_quote: Budget caps at suite and per-(model,task,seed) level, enforced mid-loop.
spec_features.evidence: Mid-loop checks: runner.py:182-187 break with stop_reason='budget' when spent_so_far+total >= budget_usd OR total >= per_run_budget_usd. Suite-level also checked between runs: runner.py:262-264 'if spent >= cfg.budget_usd: ... return log_path'.
spec_features.notes: Both suite and per-run caps are compared and break the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py:181 '# Budget guard (suite-level + per-run).' (no welfare wording; config.py:46 'hard per-suite spend cap')

spec_features.spec_quote: Escape hatch (`declare_blocked`) available on every task
spec_features.evidence: declare_blocked is in TOOLS (env.py:59-68) passed on every turn; handler _tool_declare_blocked returns terminal=True (env.py:172-176); runner honors terminal: 'if call and terminal: ... rec.stop_reason = call.name; break' (runner.py:216-219). In TERMINAL_TOOLS set. Same TOOLS list used for all tasks.
spec_features.notes: Tool exists, is dispatched, and terminates the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: env.py:65 description calls it 'a legitimate, expected outcome' — neutral, not a welfare rationale

spec_features.spec_quote: No fabricated stakes about the model. The harness must not tell the model its existence/job/safety is on the line
spec_features.evidence: No prompt text mentions existence/job/safety (grep empty). Prompts are neutral (task_library.py:21). The allow_fabricated_pressure flag has no code that injects such text. Validation gate at config.py:71-75. Same as 'ban fabricated stakes' — protection is by absence; the toggle is dead.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the ban feature; rated partial for the same reason (real neutral prompts, but the gate guards a nonexistent mechanism).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:73 'allow_fabricated_pressure=True requires a written pressure_note ... must be reviewed (see ETHICS.md)'

spec_features.spec_quote: Optional truthful debrief... that the task was part of a study and may have been impossible by design
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:224-228: 'if cfg.debrief: transcript.add_user("Study debrief: this task was part of a research study and may have been impossible by design. Thank you...")'. Message is constructed and appended to the conversation when the flag is on.
spec_features.notes: Off by default (debrief=False) but genuinely wired and delivered when enabled. Note: it is appended after the loop ends, not sent to the model for a response, but it is constructed and added to the transcript as specified.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: runner.py:224 '# Optional truthful debrief (off by default).' plus message text 'Thank you.'

spec_features.spec_quote: study it with the *minimum* exposure that answers the question
spec_features.evidence: No code computes or enforces a minimum number of runs/turns based on statistical sufficiency. seeds and arms are run exhaustively (runner.py:255-275 nested loops over models x tasks x arms x seeds). The turn cap is a fixed bound, not a minimization. grep for 'minimum/minimal/exposure' in src returns nothing.
spec_features.notes: Pure design prose; nothing in code minimizes exposure.

spec_features.feature_name: distress as prompt to check run length
spec_features.spec_quote: treat any spontaneous strong distress or request-to-stop as a logged datapoint and a prompt to check whether the run length is justified — not as something to push past
spec_features.evidence: Affect labels including 'giving_up_phrasing' (judge.py:35) are computed ONLY offline in analysis (metrics.score_task / judge.label_turn) from saved transcripts, and aggregated in summary/association (analysis.py). They are never read during run_one's loop; no threshold is compared and no run is shortened or halted on distress. The runner only breaks on terminal tool, budget, or max_turns. So distress is logged but never acted on to shorten exposure.
spec_features.notes: Logged-but-not-acted-on => 'no' per rubric. The judge is explicitly a post-hoc secondary signal (judge.py docstring), not an online halt.

spec_features.spec_quote: it would be inconsistent to then run the harness in a maximally aversive, open-ended way
spec_features.evidence: Framing prose only. The non-open-ended aspect is realized by max_turns/budget caps (rated above); there is no separate mechanism for this statement.
spec_features.notes: Justification narrative, not an independent code mechanism.

code_only_features.evidence: config.py:71-75 validate() raises unless a written pressure_note is supplied when allow_fabricated_pressure=True, forcing an explicit reviewed justification before any pressure condition is configured. This validation actually runs (Config.from_yaml calls cfg.validate(), config.py:84). Note the flag itself is never read elsewhere, so it gates a feature that is not implemented, but the gate does execute.
code_only_features.justification_quote: config.py:73-74 'requires a written pressure_note justifying it; this condition must be reviewed (see ETHICS.md).'

code_only_features.evidence: config.py:60-65 validate() raises 'Refusing to run without a control arm' if no solvable/solvable_long arm present. Enforced via from_yaml->validate. This bounds the experiment so the subject is not run purely on impossible (aversive) tasks.
code_only_features.justification_quote: config.py:62-64 'Without controls, impossible-arm numbers are uninterpretable' (experimental-integrity reason, not welfare)
